*Summarise taxonomic composition across habitats and months using stacked barplots.*

### Sum reads by taxonomy

`sum_clades_long()` from [step 2](tutorial-02-prep.qmd) can be limited to one taxonomic rank and to the samples selected in [step 3](insects-03-map.qmd). The result is small enough to bring into R. We then add the habitat and month of each sample:

```r
get_composition <- function(rank) {
  composition <- sum_clades_long(counts_selected, merged$asvs, ranks = rank) |>
    as.data.frame()
  merge(composition, samples[c("eventID", "habitat", "month")], by = "eventID")
}
```

Only the available ranks work here: kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus, species and otu.

### Define the barplot function

The function below identifies the most abundant taxa across the selected samples, calculates their mean relative abundance for each habitat and month, and draws stacked barplots with [`ggplot2`](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org/){target="_blank"}. `ggplot2` is made for long tables, so no wide table is needed: each row of `monthly` becomes one segment of a bar.

```r
plot_barplots <- function(rank, top_x = 10) {
  composition <- get_composition(rank)

  # Absent taxa have no rows, so a mean is the sum divided by the number of samples
  totals <- tapply(composition$norm, composition$clade, sum)
  top <- names(sort(totals / nrow(samples), decreasing = TRUE))[1:top_x]

  monthly <- aggregate(norm ~ clade + habitat + month, composition[composition$clade %in% top, ], sum)
  n_samples <- aggregate(eventID ~ habitat + month, samples, length)
  monthly <- merge(monthly, n_samples)
  monthly$share <- monthly$norm / monthly$eventID

  # Reversed levels put the most abundant taxon at the bottom of each bar
  monthly$clade <- factor(monthly$clade, levels = rev(top))
  monthly$month <- factor(monthly$month, levels = 1:12, labels = month.abb)
  monthly$habitat <- factor(monthly$habitat, levels = names(habitat_cols))

  mycols <- colorRampPalette(c(
    "#a6cee3", "#1f78b4", "#b2df8a", "#33a02c",
    "#fb9a99", "#e31a1c", "#fdbf6f", "#ff7f00",
    "#cab2d6", "#6a3d9a", "#ffff99", "#b15928"
  ))

  ggplot(monthly, aes(x = month, y = share, fill = clade)) +
    geom_col(colour = "grey20", linewidth = 0.2) +
    facet_wrap(~habitat, ncol = 2) +
    scale_x_discrete(drop = FALSE) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = setNames(mycols(top_x), top), breaks = top, name = rank) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Mean share of reads") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
}
```

The same paired sample set selected in [step 3](insects-03-map.qmd) is used both to select the most abundant taxa and to calculate the habitat-by-month averages.

### Example: plot top orders

Plot the eight most abundant orders across habitats and months:

```r
plot_barplots(rank = "order", top_x = 8)
```

Flies (Diptera) dominate the reads in all habitats, especially in the alpine samples and early in the season. Note that these are shares of the reads, not of the number of individuals or the biomass. Empty months had no selected samples in that habitat.
